sources.read_scope: Abstract/introduction; section 2 p4; section 5 pp14-19; not a complete proof review
sources.notes: The classification includes coverings beyond genus=d. Section 2 defines the pullback/conorm followed by norm map on degree-zero divisor classes. For odd characteristic, table cases 5 and 6 give degree-three genus-three families; case 13 gives degree-five genus-five with four consecutive Frobenius-conjugate roots; case 24 gives degree-seven genus-seven with root exponents 0,1,2,4 or 0,2,3,4. Alpha lies outside the base field. These families do not by themselves supply a matched comparison on a base-field-defined trace-zero instance.

sources.read_scope: Official Weil descent documentation, API description and example
sources.notes: WeilDescent(E,k,c) supports ordinary characteristic-two elliptic curves. It returns a covering and divisor mapping; hyperelliptic output permits Jacobian-class arithmetic. The documented non-hyperelliptic mapping requires degree-zero conversion. WeilDescentGenus and WeilDescentDegree are available. This page establishes no arbitrary odd-characteristic elliptic API.

design_inferences.statement: Before timing any descent comparator on a trace-zero subgroup, explicitly test the mapped nonzero subgroup generator remains nonzero and has the expected order. The degree-one base-field descent norm is the trace and vanishes on the trace-zero kernel.

A separately generated weak-cover example can calibrate a descent implementation, but it cannot count as a matched same-instance competitor to the E/Fq trace-zero ladder. Conditional source coverage must record applicability and the reason for exclusion, rather than fabricate a genus or timing.
